title: MCP — Reliability
description: Breakers, bulkheads, retries and the OUTCOME_UNKNOWN counter. Breaker and bulkhead state is PER INSTANCE by design — see docs/reference-architecture.md — so panels here deliberately break out by instance rather than summing, because the sum hides the one pod that is actually broken.

panels.title: Circuit breaker state by instance
panels.description: 0 closed, 1 half-open, 2 open. Broken out by instance because breakers are per-instance state: one pod with an open breaker while the rest are closed is a pod-local problem (bad DNS, exhausted connection pool), not an upstream outage. Summing these would average that signal away.

panels.title: Bulkhead queue depth
panels.description: Queued calls per bulkhead. Every configured bulkhead publishes zero at startup, so an idle group shows an idle panel rather than a blank one — a blank panel and a healthy one must not look the same.

panels.title: Bulkhead rejections
panels.description: Calls shed because a queue was full. Counts QUEUE_FULL only — a caller that cancelled while queued is not load being shed, and folding the two together would invert the diagnosis during a burst of client disconnects.

panels.title: Retry attempts by outcome
panels.description: Counts RETRIES only, not the initial attempt — every call already appears once in mcp_tool_calls_total, and counting it again here would make the retry rate unreadable against a baseline of 1.

panels.title: Retry budget exhausted
panels.description: Calls that retried and still failed, labelled by the error finally returned. This distinguishes "retried and still failed" from "failed once and was not eligible" — which look identical in mcp_tool_errors_total.

panels.title: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN rate
panels.description: The most important panel here. OUTCOME_UNKNOWN means the runtime could not determine whether a side effect happened — distinct from failure, and NOT safe to retry blindly. A non-zero rate means some callers cannot know whether their write landed.

panels.title: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN total (24h)
panels.description: The reference SLO treats any OUTCOME_UNKNOWN as worth investigating rather than as background noise, because the caller is left unable to reconcile.

panels.title: Upstream latency p99 by executor
panels.description: Time spent in the upstream call itself, split by executor type. Compare against tool latency on the Overview: a large gap is time spent in the runtime, not in the upstream.
